title: Processing single cells inside semi-permeable capsules: a generic microfluidic workflow
text:
[METHODS SECTION, moved to the front]
2. Methods
2.1 Cell preparation
Adherent cells were cultured in a culture vessel at 37 °C with 5% CO2 until confluent (placeholder: 3 days,
medium changed daily). The medium was removed and the cells were rinsed once with buffer (200 µL).
Dissociation enzyme (100 µL) was added and the cells were incubated for 5 min at 37 °C to detach them.
Quench medium (200 µL) was added and mixed gently to stop the enzyme. The cells were centrifuged at 300
g for 5 min and the supernatant was removed. The pellet was resuspended in wash buffer (500 µL) and the
wash was repeated once. The suspension was passed through a 40 µm cell strainer. Cells were counted and
viability was checked. Cells were resuspended in core solution at the loading density (placeholder: 2 x 10^6
cells/mL).

2.2 Capsule generation
The cell/core solution was co-flowed with the shell polymer solution (kept warm) and focused with fluorinated
oil containing surfactant in a flow-focusing junction to make droplets of about 70 µm (placeholder flows: core
2 µL/min, shell 2 µL/min, oil 10 µL/min). The emulsion was collected and kept on ice for 15-30 min so that the
shell gelled. The emulsion was broken by adding emulsion-breaking agent and the oil phase was removed.
Capsule shells were photocured with 405 nm light (placeholder: 30 s) in the presence of photoinitiator.
Capsules were washed three times in buffer to remove oil and free reagents and filtered through a 100 µm
strainer to remove aggregates.

2.3 Processing inside capsules
The buffer was exchanged for lysis buffer and the capsules were incubated (placeholder time and
temperature). Capsules were washed three times in wash buffer. The buffer was then exchanged for reverse
transcription mix and the capsules were incubated (placeholder time and temperature), followed by two
washes. The capsules were split into four equal portions, and index PCR was run on each portion with a
different index primer mix (placeholder number of cycles). The cDNA was released by digesting the capsule
shells with a shell-digesting enzyme (placeholder time and temperature).

2.4 Library clean-up and quality control
The library was bound to magnetic beads, washed twice with ethanol wash solution on a magnet and eluted
in water. Library concentration and fragment size were measured.

[REST OF THE PAPER]
Processing single cells inside semi-permeable capsules: a
                  generic microfluidic workflow
                A. Example and B. Placeholder (illustrative document, not a real publication)

Abstract
     Semi-permeable capsules (SPCs) let small molecules and enzymes reach cells and their nucleic
     acids while keeping large products inside, so many single cells can be processed in bulk. Here we
     describe a generic workflow, paraphrased from published SPC methods, that takes adherent cells
     through dissociation, encapsulation, photocuring, lysis, reverse transcription and index PCR to a
     sequencing-ready library. All values are placeholders for illustration, not a validated recipe.

1. Introduction
Droplet microfluidics compartmentalises single cells, but each droplet supports only one reaction mix.
Capsules with a hydrogel shell can be washed and exchanged into new reagents many times (Leonaviciene
& Mazutis, Nucleic Acids Research 2023; Baronas et al., Science 2026). This note restates the workflow in a
generic form for use as a test document.

3. Results
This is an illustrative document and reports no experimental results. A typical run is expected to give capsules
of about 70 µm with one cell or none per capsule.

References
1. Leonaviciene G., Mazutis L. RNA cytometry of single cells using semi-permeable microcapsules. Nucleic
Acids Research (2023).
2. Baronas et al. Science (2026).
